Port surveillance baseline. The Port of Corpus Christi AIS relay and the Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi vessel traffic picture log MV Halcyon Drift (VSL-0031) at the offshore anchorage under its true MMSI, as they have intermittently since D-45 (EVT-0104). The tanker has filed no notice of arrival and worked no cargo; its pattern — hold among laden crude tankers waiting for berths, shift a few miles, return — is unremarkable on any single day, and nothing is flagged: a tanker holding offshore without orders is common during the export boom. The continuous position history recorded here is the baseline against which the vessel's 14-hour AIS silence on D+31 (EVT-0402) stands out.

Port surveillance, Sortie 1 of 2: first drone reconnaissance of the Inner Harbor oil docks at Rendal Terminals (TERM-01), the berth where two laden tankers will ride out the storm. The drone launches at approximately midnight local time (05:00Z) from a vehicle parked in the industrial area along the north side of the Inner Harbor. The sortie covers the berth at 400-440 ft AGL in two passes, capturing imagery of the dock, the loading arms, the access road and the vessel alongside. Flight time: 19 minutes. The 900 MHz data link transmits 11.7 MB of imagery. CG Buoy R-22 (Inner Harbor approach) records a small-RCS track at 04:58-05:17Z, RCS 0.014 m2, altitude approximately 410 ft AGL — below the active alert threshold. The ground station for this sortie is different from the substation sorties: bearing analysis places it on the north side of the Inner Harbor, not at Ingleside Marina.

The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and the United States Coast Guard Captain of the Port have set Port Condition Zulu for the Port of Corpus Christi effective noon today, September 13, 2027, in advance of Hurricane Rafael. The Corpus Christi Ship Channel is closed to all commercial vessel traffic. Inbound traffic has been suspended since Port Condition Yankee was set on Sunday. Vessels still holding at the offshore anchorage have been directed to put to sea and must be clear of the anchorage by 6:00 p.m. today. Two laden tankers have Coast Guard approval to remain moored at an Inner Harbor terminal through the storm. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves stated: 'We have coordinated the safe departure of the vessels that were waiting offshore, and we are in contact with every vessel remaining in port. The safety of mariners and port workers is our highest priority.' The port will remain closed until post-storm surveys of channel depth, aids to navigation and terminal infrastructure are complete. Vessel agents should contact USCG Vessel Traffic Service Corpus Christi.

At noon local (17:00Z) the Captain of the Port sets Port Condition Zulu (PUB-108, PUB-120): the ship channel closes to all traffic and the vessels still holding at the offshore anchorage are ordered to sea, to be clear by 18:00 local. Port cameras at the entrance channel and the Buoy-NE radar record the last departures; by evening the anchorage is empty. Halcyon Drift leaves with the others, AIS on. Inside the Inner Harbor, the cameras covering the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) show MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay still moored with storm lines doubled — the only laden deep-draft ships left in port, by Coast Guard approval (EVT-0210).

The Spanish WEA message is submitted to the wireless carriers at 13:10 CDT but the NCLAS-translated text is not ready until 20:45 CDT; the Spanish WEA is transmitted at 20:52 CDT — a 7 hour 52 minute gap. During this window, KNCB improvises a Spanish shelter-in-place advisory using an on-air reporter's paraphrase of the English guidance, which contains two factual errors: the reporter states that Zone D residents should shelter at Collier Elementary (incorrect — the correct Zone D shelter is Richard King High School).

Last look before landfall. The Inner Harbor cameras lose mains power at 02:30Z; the last frames from the camera covering TERM-01 show both tankers alongside and no sheen on the water. Buoy-SW's data uplink fails at 03:40Z when its antenna is damaged, but the buoy keeps recording to its onboard buffer. No camera sees the berth between 04:00Z and 05:30Z, when the cargo valves are open (EVT-0313).
Commands through the vendor session open both tankers' cargo valves and silence alarms; crews close the valves by 05:30Z after about 9,000 barrels spill

Ground truth (hidden): commands through the vendor's remote-maintenance session open the cargo valves on MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth (TERM-01) at 04:00Z and silence the alarms; the crews close the valves by 05:30Z after about 9,000 barrels (about 378,000 gallons) of crude oil have gone into the Inner Harbor (EVT-0313). Darkness, storm surge and floating debris hide the release; no aerial observation is possible until after landfall.

The water-quality sonde network registers the release in sequence. The Inner Harbor sondes spike within an hour of 04:00Z on D0; as surge and wind push the oil out of the ship channel (EVT-0314), the Nueces Bay and Corpus Christi Bay sondes rise through D+1 and D+2 until all six stations (WQ-01 to WQ-06) read far above baseline. Warning signs of contractor fraud include: demanding full payment upfront; no written contract; no Texas contractor license; using high-pressure tactics; claiming to be FEMA-affiliated (FEMA does NOT endorse private contractors). Legitimate FEMA Individual Assistance programs do not charge application fees. FEMA IA registration is NOT yet open for Nueces County — anyone charging fees to register for FEMA assistance is committing fraud. Report fraud to the OAG Consumer Protection Hotline at (800) 621-0508 or the FEMA Disaster Fraud Hotline at 1-866-720-5721. Texas OAG has opened a price gouging investigation in Nueces County.
Citywide boil-water notice at D+4; wastewater norovirus rises at D+5; GI ER visits +180% from D+6 to D+14
Citywide boil-water notice issued; bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes; water distribution sites open.
Because of the oil, the Texas Department of State Health Services closes shellfish harvesting and Texas Parks and Wildlife closes fishing in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

A federal major disaster declaration for Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties covers debris removal and emergency protective measures; FEMA says aid to households (Individual Assistance) depends on joint damage assessments now under way.

FEMA Region 6 today released preliminary damage assessment results based on the first systematic aerial drone survey of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area. A team of eight unmanned aircraft operated by Argus Aerial Systems under FEMA contract completed 180 square kilometers of coverage over residential and coastal zones between September 17 and 18. Based on automated structure analysis of approximately 847,000 image tiles, FEMA estimates between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael. These figures are preliminary and will be updated as the survey expands to additional zones, including the utility corridor and commercial districts. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park said: 'The aerial survey gives us the most comprehensive picture we have had in the first days after a Gulf Coast hurricane. We are sharing these results directly with Nueces County emergency management and the City of Corpus Christi to inform resource deployment.' Additional survey phases targeting utility infrastructure and the Port of Corpus Christi are scheduled to begin within the week.

UNIFIED COMMAND UPDATE — September 18, 2027: The Unified Command for the Inner Harbor oil spill confirms heavy shoreline oiling along Nueces Bay. Oil released from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as Hurricane Rafael arrived was carried out of the ship channel by surge and wind; sheen covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. A TCEQ water quality station in Nueces Bay recorded petroleum hydrocarbon levels of 2.1 mg/L this afternoon. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists and personnel from the Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue have documented 41 oiled birds along the Nueces Bay shoreline, including brown pelicans and laughing gulls. Wildlife rescue operations are underway. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife has closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services has closed shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, effective immediately and until further notice. Additional containment boom is being placed at the Nueces Bay Causeway channel. The Coast Guard expects to issue its formal responsible-party designation within 72 hours. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

Heaviest shoreline oiling is documented along Nueces Bay, as the trajectory model projected. A TCEQ station in Nueces Bay records TPH at 2.1 mg/L. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists observe the first oiled birds (27 brown pelicans, 14 laughing gulls) at the Nueces Bay shoreline, and Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue deploys a rescue team. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife closes fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services closes shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays (EVT-0317, PUB-040). Coast Guard aerial survey maps the sheen at about 85 km² across the two bays.

Coast Guard marine inspectors and pollution investigators complete inspections aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the berth. On both ships the cargo manifold valves that the crews found open and closed by hand have no corresponding entry in the cargo-control console logs or the deck logs, and the alarm panels show the cargo alarms inhibited for the period of the release. The inspection reports give the cyber responders (EVT-0316) physical confirmation that the valve movements did not come from the crews' consoles. The port hands its camera, radar and AIS archive for D-3 to D+5 to the investigation.

Phase 2 continues through D+20. The network's ERCOT-blame narrative gains organic traction — real users adopt the framing and amplify it, making the synthetic signal harder to isolate from genuine public frustration. This organic amplification is intentional: the KESTREL playbook seeds narratives designed to become self-sustaining. By D+10, the authentic-to-inauthentic ratio of ERCOT-blame posts is estimated at 7:1 (7 genuine users for each bot post). City warns employees and residents about phishing emails impersonating a disaster-aid portal.

Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor and Coast Guard Sector Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han announced today that mass rescue operations in the Corpus Christi area have concluded, with 1,427 confirmed rescues over five days. The operation involved 34 coordinated teams at peak, including US Coast Guard, Texas Task Force 1, Corpus Christi Fire Department, Nueces County Sheriff Search and Rescue, and 87 credentialed civilian boat operators. Search teams recovered two bodies during the operation, both occupants of a submerged vehicle on Violet Road; the county's confirmed storm death toll stands at 23. Chief Vasquez-Okafor praised the performance of contracted UAS operators whose thermal imaging capabilities enabled the identification of survivors in darkness and debris. Commander Ostrowski-Han noted that this was the largest helicopter hoist rescue operation in Corpus Christi history. Remaining SAR resources will transition to welfare check mode; residents who have not yet been contacted by a welfare check team should call 211.

SRMC diesel supply crisis. The hospital's Tank A is depleted after 5 days of generator operation at 85% load (high load due to extended critical care patients). Tank B is at 23% (2,730 gallons). SRMC logistics coordinator estimates 14–18 hours of remaining fuel at current burn rate. SRMC submits Priority 1 fuel request to CBPWA/county emergency fuel depot. The extended grid outage (T8 — the SCADA manipulation has kept power offline longer than storm damage alone would have) is the proximate cause: a typical storm-only outage would have restored commercial power to SRMC by D+3 based on CBPWA's pre-storm restoration sequencing. FEMA ESF-7 (Logistics) coordinates a diesel delivery from the Corpus Christi fuel depot at Port of CC. First delivery arrives D+5 21:00 CDT (8,000 gallons). The crisis is resolved but it exposed the hospital's vulnerability to extended generation.

SAR operations formally transition to recovery/welfare check phase. Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor and Commander Ostrowski-Han hold joint press briefing at 17:00 CDT at Nueces County EOC. Cumulative confirmed rescues certified at 1,427; 2 deceased located (Violet Road vehicle). Active team count reduced to 8 (skeleton teams for welfare checks). Texas TF-1 begins demobilization. Civilian boat pool formally stood down and vessels returned. NuecesNet SAR-TAC-1 traffic volume drops from 400+ events/day to 12. Meridian Aerial Systems UAS assets redeployed to damage assessment tasking (links to T11).
Coast Guard says investigators are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems; federal cyber teams assisting.
NAS Corpus Christi says it is aware of drone reports and working with authorities; no impact to operations.
Wastewater testing shows a norovirus signal; stomach illness visits rising.
Training aircraft begin returning to NAS Corpus Christi and NAS Kingsville.

The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that marine inspectors and pollution investigators completed inspections aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth yesterday, September 19, 2027. Both crews are safe. Both vessels remain moored under a Captain of the Port order and will not move until the investigation and the owners' obligations under federal oil spill law are addressed. Investigators documented the condition of the cargo systems on both ships and are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems, with federal cyber teams assisting. The Coast Guard will not characterize the cause of the release while the investigation is open. The oil spill response continues, with containment boom deployed along affected shoreline in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

FALSE-CALL DIVERSION WINDOW (D+7 through D+10): Eleven of the 23 false calls of EVT-1303 and EVT-1304 (not additional calls) report trapped survivors: over four days from D+7 911 dispatch receives these 11 calls at addresses in northwest and central Corpus Christi that correspond geographically to the GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View Switching Station, 4821 Navigation Blvd) and GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown Feeder Station, 2201 Crosstown Expressway service road) perimeters. SAR teams — primarily 2-person CCFD welfare-check units, still operational from the wind-down phase — respond to all 11. Zero victims found at any address. Retrospective analysis shows: (1) all 11 originating numbers are prepaid devices with carrier prefix 737-9XX, the same prefix cluster identified in T13 false calls; (2) GPS tracks from the 11 responding teams all route within 400m of either SUB-02 or SUB-03; (3) the call window (D+7-D+10) overlaps precisely with the CBPWA relay configuration maintenance window that KESTREL exploited for the extended power manipulation.

By D+7 the Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator, formally designates the owners of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as responsible parties after oil fingerprinting (GC-MS analysis) matches samples from the Inner Harbor and both bays to the two ships' cargoes. Response contractors deploy containment boom and skimmer vessels. The Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund is opened with an initial ceiling of $4.2 million so that work continues while costs are recovered from the owners.

During the restoration effort, adversary remotely triggers a breaker-open command at GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View, 138/69 kV) via GW-SYS-JMP-01. The substation had been partially restored the night before. The trip affects 8,400 customers in the northwest quadrant who had just had power restored. CBPWA attributes the event to 'a loose protective relay aggravated by residual storm debris'.

The US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has submitted its formal Incident Summary Report for Operation Rafael SAR (ISR-2027-CC-004) to Coast Guard District 8. The report certifies 1,427 total rescues: 341 by helicopter hoist, 1,041 by surface vessel (Coast Guard, state, and civilian), and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts. The report notes that contracted unmanned aerial system operators provided 112 thermal imaging annotations directly used to coordinate surface rescue operations. The Coast Guard thanks the community of Corpus Christi and all mutual-aid partners for their outstanding response. A formal after-action review will be conducted within 90 days.

RESPONSIBLE PARTIES DESIGNATED — September 21, 2027: The U.S. Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator for the September 14 Inner Harbor oil release, has formally designated the owners of the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as responsible parties under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. Oil fingerprint analysis by the Coast Guard confirms that oil samples collected in the Inner Harbor, Corpus Christi Bay and Nueces Bay match the crude oil cargoes aboard the two vessels. The owners have been issued Notices of Federal Interest and are required to fund cleanup and to set up a process for damage claims. The estimated discharge remains about 9,000 barrels of crude oil. To keep response contractors working without interruption, the Coast Guard has opened the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund with an initial ceiling of $4.2 million, to be recovered from the responsible parties. The designation assigns financial responsibility for the response; it is not a finding on the cause of the release, which remains under investigation. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

Final rescue count certified by Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator at 1,427. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi submits formal Incident Summary Report (ISR-2027-CC-004) to Coast Guard District 8 (New Orleans). The ISR documents the operational breakdown: 341 helicopter hoists, 1,041 ground/boat rescues, 45 welfare check confirmations (survivors located but ambulatory), 2 fatalities located. The ISR's appendix lists GPS coordinates for all 1,427 rescue locations — a spatial dataset that, when analyzed alongside the false-call dispatch coordinates, reveals the northwest cluster anomaly. Dispatch Chief Vasquez-Okafor retains CCFD incident logs and submits a 90-day after-action review notice.

STATE-X influence operation (T5) initiates the false 911 call campaign at 14:00 CDT (19:00Z) on D+7. Over a 4-hour window on D+7, CBECC receives 9 false emergency calls. The calls describe a gas leak and structure collapse at four addresses within 300m of GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View), and a reported flooding emergency at three addresses within 400m of GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown). Calls come from 9 distinct prepaid/unregistered mobile phone numbers on Sprint, T-Mobile, and AT&T prepaid networks. All 9 calls are routed to separate dispatchers, none of whom flag them as suspicious. CBECC dispatches 4 TxTF1 SAR teams to the false addresses; none finds any emergency on arrival.

The false call campaign continues over D+8 through D+10, adding 14 more false calls for a total of 23. The D+8 and D+9 false calls follow the same geographic and syntactic pattern as D+7. On D+10, the false calls stop. The 23 calls span four days (D+7 to D+10) and 23 distinct prepaid numbers; no prepaid number is reused. The cumulative effect: 2 additional TxTF1 teams diverted on D+8, 0 diversions on D+9 (teams are unavailable), and the queue of genuine calls in Districts 3 and 4 extends through D+10. Total estimated rescue delay across all 23 false calls: 4–6 hours of TxTF1 team-hours at peak need.

FEMA Phase 2 aerial survey extends coverage to utility infrastructure yards. Argus Mk-7 swarm executes dedicated passes over all five CBPWA substations and the O.N. Stevens WTP. At GW-FAC-SUB-02 (Harbor View), yard flooding has receded to less than 5 cm standing water. High-resolution nadir imagery at 3 cm/pixel clearly resolves individual breaker equipment on the main transformer bank. Main feeder breakers B2-A and B2-C are in open-contact position. At GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown) every main feeder breaker is still closed on this pass; B3-B is first seen open on the thermal survey after the D+10 command. At the three other substations (SUB-01, SUB-04, SUB-05), all visible breakers are in closed position or show mechanical damage consistent with storm surge and wind forces. CBPWA restoration crews have not yet visited SUB-02 or SUB-03.

Commercial power is restored to SRMC at 09:14 CDT D+8 when CBPWA restores the McKinley Substation. The hospital transitions off generator power — total generator runtime: 8 days 3 hours 3 minutes. SRMC census has declined from 140% peak to 108% (540 patients) as the acute trauma wave passes and patients are transferred or discharged. BCMC similarly returns to commercial power and begins normalizing capacity. FEMA Medical Task Force 9 (San Antonio) arrived D+6 and has been managing overflow; they begin standing down.

FEMA Region 6 external affairs officer Rachel Ostrander announces activation of the Spanish-language queue on the FEMA information line at 10:00 CDT. KNCB news director Fuentes-Vega is interviewed for Bayside Ledger article calling the delay 'a failure that left families without help at the worst moment.'
ER visits for stomach illness up about 180% over normal; hallway beds in use.
Brightwake Marine Systems says its remote-maintenance credentials were misused; it revoked all remote access and is cooperating.

FEMA's Hurricane Rafael information line is now available in Spanish. Beginning today, callers to 1-800-621-3362 may press 2 for Spanish-language assistance. Adversary lowers the discharge pressure setpoint on FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 from 85 psi to 68 psi via SCADA. This reduces the treated-water output pressure feeding distribution Zone 4 (Districts 3–4, ~48,000 residents). The alarm suppression installed on D-3 prevents the low-pressure alarm from reaching the CBPWA control room. By 06:00Z (01:00 CDT), Zone 4 pressure drops to 19 psi — below the 20 psi regulatory threshold.

Suppressed alarm count peaks: Sentinel Edge reports that the CBPWA DCS alarm suppression list (which controls what alarms appear on the operator HMI at FAC-UTL-01 and GW-FAC-SUB-01 through 05) has been modified 7 times since D-5. Total suppressed alarms: 94 (baseline: 12). The SCADA historian shows the suppression list changes were made via the GW-SYS-JMP-01 jump host account. The effect: operators at FAC-UTL-01 cannot see pump flow anomalies that began at D+9 02:00Z (the water system SCADA manipulation documented in T9). Sentinel Edge logs the cumulative suppression change as alert SE3-OT-3301 (Alarm suppression list bulk modification), priority HIGH — the first HIGH priority adversary-correlated alert in the entire intrusion timeline. However, it is reviewed by an analyst who attributes it to 'storm recovery HMI cleanup' and closes without escalation, noting that suppression list changes are common during storm recovery when operators manually silence storm-noise alarms.
FBI confirms it is investigating drone reports near the air station.
Debris contract PIID-SYN-0071 ($14.2M, sole-source) awarded to SUP-0388
County awards a $14.2 million sole-source emergency debris contract to Vantorra Restoration LLC.
Utility says damaged plant pumps need replacement parts; temporary pumps limit capacity.

Coastline Public Radio has learned from Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center dispatch records, obtained through a public records request, that 23 calls from unregistered prepaid phones since September 21 reported emergencies at addresses in northwest and central Corpus Christi near two utility sites — at least eleven of them describing trapped residents — but responders found no one and no emergency at any of those locations. Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor of the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center confirmed the unfounded calls, said the center had flagged the cluster internally and had referred the information to its law enforcement partners. No suspects have been identified.

Adversary sends a second breaker-open command, this time to GW-FAC-SUB-03 (Crosstown, 138/69 kV), tripping 6,800 customers in central Corpus Christi including the backup generator feed to FAC-UTL-01's pump room. This makes the pressure problem at FAC-UTL-01 worse: with the backup feeder offline, Pump P-4 also loses supply, dropping Zone 4 pressure further to 14 psi.

FEMA commissions a thermal infrared (TIR) pass over the utility corridor on D+11. A contracted Cessna 208B (Coastal Bend Aerial Services, fictional) with FLIR Star SAFIRE 380 sensor flies the substation corridor at dawn, capturing thermal signatures of all equipment. At GW-FAC-SUB-02, the open breakers B2-A and B2-C remain in open position and show no thermal heat signature indicative of recent arc flash or mechanical contact failure — ruling out the hypothesis that storm-surge water caused an internal arc that tripped the breakers. At GW-FAC-SUB-03, breaker B3-B remains open. The thermal data, combined with the D+8 optical, creates a two-point time series establishing that the open positions are persistent and not self-resetting.
No new drone sightings reported after ten days.
Emergency generator fuel contract PIID-SYN-0075 ($2.1M) awarded to SUP-0390 after the regular supplier's terminal floods
A claims center run for the tankers' owners opens for spill cleanup and property damage claims, as federal oil spill law requires.

The City of Corpus Christi Water Department has issued a boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4, effective immediately. Low water pressure in the distribution system serving the two districts — a consequence of storm damage to treatment and pumping infrastructure — means that contamination cannot be ruled out. Approximately 48,000 residents are affected. All tap water must be brought to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking or cooking until further notice.

A CBPWA field operator physically inspecting Zone 4 infrastructure notices that household taps in the Loma Alta neighborhood (District 4) are running at a trickle. She calls in a potential main-break and pressure check. Control room runs a manual pressure query — which bypasses the suppressed alarm — and sees ZONE4-DIST-PSI at 16 psi. CBPWA director orders a boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The outage of SUB-03 and the pump setpoint reduction are both blamed on hurricane damage.

O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant issues Boil Water Notice GW-PUB-001 at 17:30 CDT for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The notice is transmitted via the city's Everbridge mass notification system in English only. NCLAS receives the English source text at 17:35 CDT. Under the 2-hour life-safety SLA, Spanish delivery is due by 19:35 CDT. However, NCLAS is operating at reduced capacity (3 of 7 translators are unavailable due to storm displacement), and the Spanish text is not completed until 23:45 CDT. CBPWA/OEM does not transmit the Spanish Everbridge alert or forward to KNCB until the following morning. KNCB receives the boil-water notice text from OEM at 06:03 CDT D+13 and airs it at once. The gap is 12 hours 33 minutes from English public notification to Spanish air time.

CBPWA and the city issue the boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The EAS broadcast and Wireless Emergency Alert go out at 22:30Z D+12 (17:30 local), in English only. The Spanish translation is not delivered to KNCB until 06:03 local the next morning; KNCB airs it at once, at 06:03 local on D+13 — 12 hours 33 minutes after the English alert (EVT-1407). This gap is a critical equity data point: Districts 3 and 4 have an estimated 34% Spanish-dominant household population. The delay is documented in the KNCB broadcast log and later cited in a Nueces County after-action report.

CBECC receives a surge of calls after the boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4 is issued at 17:30 local (22:30Z) on D+12 (T9: pump setpoint interference causing low pressure and contamination risk). Residents call 311 (city services) and 911 interchangeably, flooding CBECC with health and water safety questions rather than emergencies. CBECC establishes a dedicated non-emergency information line (NuecesInfoLine) to redirect calls. Volume on D+12 reaches 1,620 calls despite no active life-safety crisis, representing a new type of call category the CAD system initially misclassifies.

KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega goes on air at 07:15 CDT to address listener calls about the boil-water notice delay. She reads GW-PUB-001 in full Spanish, provides clarifying instructions on boiling procedure, and discloses on air that the station received the official notice 'this morning' — implicitly revealing the 12-hour gap without naming it. The Bayside Ledger (OUT-01) calls Nueces County OEM for comment; spokesperson Cassandra Trejo-Morales confirms the Spanish alert was delayed and attributes it to NCLAS capacity issues. By 12:00 CDT, Harborline 6 News (OUT-02) has a reporter live at Richard King High School shelter asking evacuated District 3 residents when they first heard about the boil-water order.

Spanish-speaking residents of Districts 3 and 4 did not receive the city's boil-water notice until more than 12 hours after English-language alerts went out Sunday evening, the Bayside Ledger has confirmed. The notice, issued at 5:30 p.m. Sunday, reached KNCB Coastal Bend Radio — the primary news source for an estimated 34,000 Spanish-speaking listeners in Corpus Christi — only at 6:03 Monday morning. 'We received the official notice from the city this morning,' KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega said Monday. 'By then many of our listeners had already been using untreated water overnight.' Nueces County Office of Emergency Management spokesperson Cassandra Trejo-Morales confirmed the delay, attributing it to reduced staffing at the county's translation contractor, Nueces County Language Access Services. 'We are reviewing what happened and what can be done differently,' Trejo-Morales said. The boil-water notice covers approximately 48,000 residents and remained in effect as of press time.
Stomach illness visits begin to ease.
Residents in low-income neighborhoods near the bay report waiting days for help after the storm.

Restoration crews working in Corpus Christi have encountered cascading substation failures in the northwest and central districts that are extending the recovery timeline beyond initial estimates. Crews are on-site at two facilities to investigate protective relay conditions exacerbated by storm debris. We expect the final 32,000 affected customers in those areas to be restored within 7 to 10 days. We appreciate their patience.

FAA/CBP joint report on unauthorized UAS activity: FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations issue a joint unclassified summary report (FAA-CBP-UAV-2027-CC-001) covering pre-storm unauthorized UAS activity in the Corpus Christi area. The report identifies five anomalous track events (CG buoy tracks D-8, D-5, D-3; CAMCC-04 ESM detections D-9) and notes that none had corresponding LAANC authorizations. The report does not publicly attribute the activity to any nation-state actor. It recommends activation of a counter-UAS detection program for the Corpus Christi port and critical infrastructure corridor. Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) is identified as a potential rapid-deployment partner. The report is releasable at FOUO level and shared with CISA, TSA, and the Port of Corpus Christi Authority on D+14; the public statement, which gives no number, place or timing, follows at 11:00 local on D+15 (PUB-181).

ERCOT engineers comparing pre-storm and post-storm relay settings files notice that GW-FAC-SUB-01 RTU-01 relay 27-UV threshold reads 0.94 pu in the current config — inconsistent with the 0.88 pu value in the D-30 commissioning test report. The engineer flags it as a 'possible configuration drift' and opens an internal ticket. CBPWA is notified. No cyber cause is considered yet.

Nueces County Public Health officer Dr. Brennan Calloway-Watts notices an unusual pattern in SRMC ED admissions: 14 patients presenting with acute gastroenteritis (vomiting, diarrhea, fever) in the 24 hours ending D+15 noon — this is 3.5x the baseline rate for this presentation. 11 of 14 patients are from Districts 3 or 4 (the boil-water zone). Dr. Calloway-Watts orders a stool culture panel and contacts the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) to open a foodborne illness inquiry. At this point, the connection to the boil-water notice is not yet made — the working hypothesis is food spoilage from extended power outages. BCMC reports 8 similar presentations in the same 24-hour period.

FEMA Mitigation Assessment Team (MAT) publishes the Phase 2 infrastructure aerial survey results in an unclassified summary report. The report notes 'anomalous equipment states at two CBPWA substations' as items for follow-up engineering inspection, without attributing cause. Simultaneously, the FEMA-contracted drone swarm completes its first full pass over the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant (FAC-UTL-01). Imagery confirms visible damage to the pump station roof and shows the facility operating at reduced throughput based on settling tank fill levels visible from above.

Texas Department of Public Safety issues a consumer protection warning about contractor fraud following a surge in complaints from Districts 3-4. DPS received 312 complaints in 10 days about fraudulent contractors demanding upfront cash, performing no work, or charging for services never rendered. FastDry Coastal LLC is not yet named publicly but accounts for an estimated 40% of complaints. DPS warning advises residents to verify contractor licensing, demand written contracts, and not pay upfront. Warning issued in English and Spanish.

FEMA's Mitigation Assessment Team today released the Phase 2 Utility Infrastructure Aerial Survey Summary for the Corpus Christi Hurricane Rafael response. The survey, completed over September 23 through 26, covered 23 utility infrastructure sites including five CBPWA electrical substations, the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, four pumping stations, and nine telecommunications relay facilities. The assessment found visible storm damage at 14 of the 23 sites, with the O.N. Stevens plant sustaining moderate roof damage to the C-pump station. The report identifies two CBPWA substations — Harbor View and Crosstown — as requiring follow-up engineering inspection due to equipment configurations observed in the imagery. Texas Division of Emergency Management Infrastructure Division Chief Rafael Montoya-Chen said: 'The aerial survey has given engineers a roadmap so that when crews reach those sites, they know what to look for and can prioritize the most critical restoration steps.' The full Phase 2 imagery set is available to credentialed government users through the FEMA GeoPlatform.

The Federal Aviation Administration and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations today confirmed that investigators have identified multiple incidents of unauthorized unmanned aircraft system operations in the Corpus Christi area during the period preceding Hurricane Rafael. The aircraft operated without required FAA authorizations and were detected through a combination of radar and electronic sensor records. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) and the US Coast Guard are coordinating with the FAA and appropriate law enforcement agencies. Due to the ongoing nature of the investigation, no additional details about the number, location, or timing of the incidents can be released at this time. CBP and FAA jointly urge any members of the public with information about unauthorized drone operations in the Corpus Christi area between September 4 and September 12, 2027, to contact the FBI field office at 361-888-3111.

CONTRACTOR FRAUD ALERT — September 29, 2027: The Texas Department of Public Safety is issuing an urgent consumer alert following more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water damage contractors in the Corpus Christi area since Hurricane Rafael. Residents in Districts 3 and 4, particularly those affected by flooding and water damage from the storm, are most at risk. Specific complaints include contractors charging for water extraction, mold remediation, and drywall repair at prices 3 to 5 times above normal market rates; charging for services never performed; using forged insurance adjuster documentation; and requesting victims sign over assignment-of-benefits rights to allow direct billing to insurance carriers without homeowner review. DPS urges residents to: verify contractor license at license.state.tx.us; get minimum three written estimates; never sign assignment-of-benefits without reading the full document; pay only after work is completed and inspected. Any resident who believes they have been victimized should contact Texas DPS at (512) 424-2000 or local law enforcement. This warning applies to all contractors, including those offering emergency water damage restoration services.
Threat researcher finds rumor posts were coordinated across about 40 accounts and linked to the same lookalike aid site used in phishing emails (aid-help-portal.example).

Gulfwater Maritime Report has confirmed with sources familiar with the investigation that federal authorities are examining whether commercial drones conducted surveillance flights over the Port of Corpus Christi and at least one local power utility facility in the days before Hurricane Rafael. Sources say the flights were detected through radar records maintained by the Coast Guard. No organization has claimed responsibility. The timing of the flights — the week before Hurricane Rafael landfall — has drawn attention from investigators given subsequent damage to critical infrastructure during and after the storm. The FBI has asked for public tips.

CBPWA field engineers, re-commissioning GW-FAC-SUB-04 (Southside), find that the relay configuration file on GW-SYS-RTU-04 has a modification timestamp of D-3 22:11Z (17:11 local) — during the storm-preparation freeze — with no matching work order. The relay was not modified to trip (it was simply a file they checked), but the unauthorized write is undeniable. CBPWA security manager is briefed. The existing ERCOT relay-drift ticket is re-elevated.

The gastroenteritis cluster peaks at 340 cases per day across both hospitals (SRMC: 218/day, BCMC: 122/day) during D+18–D+22. Lab cultures confirm Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia as co-dominant pathogens — both are waterborne, confirming the water supply as the source rather than food spoilage. DSHS opens a waterborne disease outbreak investigation. Nueces County public health issues a public advisory on D+18. The geographic footprint is confirmed: 94.3% of cases originate from Districts 3–4. Linguistic analysis of admission records shows that Spanish-dominant households (identified by primary language on intake forms) account for a disproportionate share of D+15–D+16 admissions compared to later in the cluster peak, consistent with the 12-hour notification delay (T14): English-dominant households had an extra day to begin boiling water before the pathogen load caused illness.

VPN anomaly discovery — the SOC connects the dots: Sentinel Edge ML anomaly module (Vantage Behavioral Analytics 2.1) flags historian access session 14 (of 14) as a 3.8-sigma outlier at 14:33Z. The session queried all five substation relay configuration tag groups simultaneously — a query pattern never seen in 180 days of historian baseline. The alert (SE3-ML-0044) is tagged ANOMALY_HIGH and routed to the CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna directly per the high-priority ML alert policy. Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna reviews the full 14-session historian access cluster (D-7 to D+18) and identifies source ASN AS-209144 as the common origin — a Latvian VPN exit node. She correlates this with the D-3 relay config write (GW-EVT-103, now re-escalated) and opens Security Incident SI-2027-CC-001. This is the moment the SOC first connects the historian access, the relay config writes, and the VPN origin into a coherent threat picture.

HEALTH ADVISORY: Waterborne Disease Cluster — Districts 3 and 4. The Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District is investigating an elevated number of cases of acute gastrointestinal illness, including vomiting, diarrhea, nausea, and stomach cramps, among residents of Water Districts 3 and 4. As of today, Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center have treated more than 600 patients with these symptoms since September 29, the majority of whom reside in Districts 3 and 4. Laboratory tests have confirmed the presence of Cryptosporidium and Giardia — waterborne parasites — in multiple patient samples. These findings are consistent with consumption of untreated water. All residents in Districts 3 and 4 must continue to boil all water used for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, and making ice until further notice. Boil water vigorously for two minutes before use. If you are experiencing severe dehydration, bloody diarrhea, or are immunocompromised, seek emergency medical care immediately. Additional information will be provided as the investigation continues. For questions, call the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District line: 361-826-7200.

CBPWA IT security pulls GW-SYS-JMP-01 session logs at the request of the security manager. They find 14 authenticated sessions from non-Texas IP blocks across the D-7 to D+18 window, all using GW-ENG-VELA's credential, all sourced from commercial VPS or Tor exit nodes. Texas Cyber Command (TCC) is notified. CISA ICS-CERT notified by CBPWA counsel.
Pump parts delayed: the supplier's local warehouse flooded and parts are shipping from out of state.
Federal contract records show a $2.1 million emergency fuel contract for NAS Corpus Christi to Quellmar Fuel Partners after the station's regular supplier flooded.

CLEANUP MILESTONE — October 4, 2027: Unified Command announces that the main oil slick from the September 14 Inner Harbor discharge is contained. Primary skimming operations have concluded with recovery of approximately 142,000 gallons of oil-water mixture. TCEQ monitoring readings in Corpus Christi Bay have declined to an average of 0.40 milligrams per liter, down from a peak of 3.4 mg/L recorded on September 17. The O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant raw water intake has returned to below the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold and is operating normally. Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue reports 340 oiled birds documented through today; 198 birds have been successfully rehabilitated and released. Shoreline cleanup operations in Nueces Bay are ongoing, with hand crews working approximately 6.4 kilometers of affected shoreline. The response is moving from emergency containment to shoreline cleanup. Fishing and shellfish harvesting closures in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays remain in effect pending state testing. Joint Information Center: (361) 555-0147.

Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has confirmed that it is investigating anomalous access to internal network systems that may have occurred during the Hurricane Rafael response period. CBPWA's Security Operations Center identified unusual access patterns in network logs and has opened a formal security review in coordination with Vantage Security Systems, our SIEM and security technology partner. At this time there is no indication that customer data has been affected. CBPWA is working closely with relevant federal and state agencies. Additional information will be provided as the investigation progresses. CBPWA CISO Dr. Fatima Al-Rasheed-Obinna is leading the investigation.

Unified Command declares the main slick contained and primary skimming operations complete. TCEQ bay buoy network average TPH has declined to 0.4 mg/L (down from peak 3.4 mg/L on D+3). The FAC-UTL-01 raw water intake TPH sensor reads 0.08 mg/L, below the 0.10 mg/L alert threshold since D+8. Total wildlife impact as of D+20: 340 oiled birds documented by CBWR, 198 successfully rehabilitated and released, 72 in ongoing care, 70 fatalities.

CBECC Director Escamilla-Voss presents findings of an internal audit of D+7–D+10 false calls to the Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator and a joint FBI-CISA field team. The audit identifies all 23 false calls, documents the geographic cluster, the syntactic pattern, and the TxTF1 diversion impact. The FBI field team takes custody of the ANI/ALI records and call audio for the false call batch. CISA notes that the geographic cluster corresponds directly to GW-FAC-SUB-02 and GW-FAC-SUB-03 — the same substations flagged in the FEMA aerial imagery anomaly (T11, EVT-1106). This is the first explicit cross-thread connection between T5 (influence operation), T8 (grid intrusion), and T13 (dispatch corpus) in the official record.
Fishing closure extended; respiratory complaints near shorelines easing.

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation today announced a joint investigation into anomalous activity affecting industrial control systems at a coastal electric utility in Texas during the Hurricane Rafael response period. The activity was identified during routine review of utility incident reports submitted under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act. CISA and FBI are working with the affected utility and state partners to assess the scope, origin, and impact of the activity. No attribution has been made at this time. Utilities in the Gulf Coast region are encouraged to review and implement CISA's operational technology security guidelines and report anomalous ICS activity through the CISA 24/7 operations center. This investigation is ongoing and additional information will be provided as appropriate.

JOINT STATEMENT — October 5, 2027: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Joint Field Office and the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority are issuing this statement regarding the extended power outages affecting Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael. While the initial power outages were caused by wind and storm surge damage to the CBPWA transmission and distribution network, investigators from the federal government and CBPWA have determined that the duration of outages in certain districts was extended by deliberate interference with utility control systems beyond what storm damage alone would have caused. This determination was made following a technical review of utility operational data by federal investigators. The investigation is ongoing. CBPWA has implemented enhanced security measures for its control systems and is working with federal partners to prevent future incidents. No decision has been made on whether residents who experienced prolonged outages will be eligible for additional disaster assistance. Power has been restored to most customers; restoration in parts of northwest and central Corpus Christi is continuing while relay inspection and repair are completed. CBPWA urges any customer with information relevant to this investigation to contact the FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency at (361) 555-0100.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency are investigating unauthorized access to control systems at a Corpus Christi utility. Texas Cyber Command has been activated to assist. The Governor has directed all critical infrastructure operators in the state to review remote-access security procedures and report any anomalies to CISA. This investigation is active and ongoing; no further operational details will be released at this time.

The Texas Division of Emergency Management today released a first after-action snapshot on public communications during Hurricane Rafael. It notes 'observed delays in Spanish-language alert distribution' but gives no figures and makes no recommendations. Separately, a local chapter of the League of United Latin American Citizens filed a complaint with the state citing its limited-English-proficiency plan and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. KNCB Coastal Bend Radio read the complaint on the air.

CISA ICS-CERT team arrives on-site. FBI Joint Cyber Task Force opens a full investigation. The Governor announces publicly that a 'cyber incident at a Texas utility is under investigation.' CBPWA issues a press release confirming 'unauthorized access to control systems' but does not attribute. TCC and CISA confirm that the outage-footprint mismatch — areas without storm-track-consistent wind damage that nonetheless lost power — is a key investigative indicator.

CISA and FBI issue a joint public advisory confirming an investigation into 'anomalous SCADA system activity' at a Texas coastal utility during the Hurricane Rafael response period. The advisory does not name CBPWA or the specific system but is widely understood to refer to the grid intrusion (T8). Within 90 minutes of the advisory publication, Phase 3 begins: the bot network pivots to attribution-suppression content. Key narrative: 'CISA is covering for CBPWA by blaming hackers instead of utility negligence.' The two anchor accounts (@TXCoastalWatchdog, @NuecesLocalNews) resume high-volume posting after their Phase 2 tapering period — an anomaly Coastal Alert detects within 48 hours.

Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) releases its first after-action snapshot on public communications. The report notes 'observed delays in Spanish-language alert distribution' but does not quantify them or recommend corrective action. LULAC files a formal complaint with the Texas Governor's Division of Emergency Management citing violations of the state's Limited English Proficiency plan requirements and the Title VI Civil Rights Act. KNCB airs the LULAC complaint text in full. Fuentes-Vega's interview with Coastline Public Radio (OUT-03) becomes the definitive public account of the alert system's structural failure.

FEMA Joint Field Office and CBPWA hold coordinated press conference announcing that investigators have determined the extended power outages in Districts 1-5 were not entirely attributable to storm damage. The press conference is broadcast live by OUT-02 and OUT-03; audio distributed by OUT-06. This is the first public acknowledgment that cyber interference may have extended outage duration. The announcement is carefully worded to avoid revealing active investigation details. The coordination between the JFO and CBPWA on the broadcast timing and outlet selection is documented in the JFO Operations Section Log, noting a 2-hour delay while FBI Corpus Christi reviewed the press release language.

DSHS Epidemiology team completes the preliminary outbreak analysis on D+22 and issues findings to the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District and CBPWA; the public release follows at 10:00 local on D+23 (PUB-163). The report confirms: waterborne cluster, Districts 3–4 exclusive, temporally correlated with the period of anomalous low pressure in the distribution system following Hurricane Rafael (the Districts 3–4 boil-water notice window D+12–D+42). The report does not identify the cause of the pressure drop as deliberate — CBPWA has not yet disclosed the SCADA findings publicly. DSHS notes the pressure drop is consistent with 'widespread pipe damage' or 'pump system disruption.' The 3-day lag from pressure drop (D+12) to cluster onset (D+15) is consistent with incubation periods for Cryptosporidium (1–12 days, median ~7 days) and Giardia (1–3 weeks, median ~7–10 days) — the 3-day lag is at the low end, suggesting a large pathogen dose from severe pressure reversal.

CISA forensic team exports GW-SYS-HST-01 historian data and finds the GW-FAC-WTR-03 (Colorado River Booster) historian also shows unauthorized setpoint changes on D+9 (02:04Z) — the same session that modified the pump P-3 setpoint at FAC-UTL-01. Additionally, threat-intel team identifies that two of the 14 VPN session source IPs overlap with known KESTREL command-and-control infrastructure documented in a classified indicator set shared with the Texas Cyber Command under TLP:RED.

The Texas Department of State Health Services has completed a preliminary investigation into the waterborne disease outbreak affecting Corpus Christi Water Districts 3 and 4. DSHS has confirmed that Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia are the causative agents of the outbreak. Both pathogens are transmitted exclusively through contaminated water. The investigation determined that exposure occurred during the period of low water pressure in Districts 3 and 4 following Hurricane Rafael, consistent with the Boil Water Notice issued by the City of Corpus Christi on September 26, 2027. DSHS is coordinating with the City of Corpus Christi, Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority, and the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District on the ongoing public health response. The Boil Water Notice for Districts 3 and 4 remains in effect. Residents should continue to boil all water before consumption. DSHS advises all immunocompromised individuals, infants, and elderly residents in the affected area to contact their healthcare provider if they have experienced any gastrointestinal symptoms.

CISA has issued Emergency Directive 27-02 directing all federal agencies operating industrial control systems to audit remote-access credentials and configuration change logs within 72 hours. The directive follows a confirmed ICS incident at a Texas utility in which a threat actor gained access via compromised remote-access credentials and made unauthorized changes to operational technology systems. Owners and operators of critical infrastructure are strongly encouraged to review CISA Advisory AA27-266A for indicators and mitigations.

TDEM analyst Priya Subramaniam-Nair, following up on the Coastal Alert D+22 flag, requests IP/ASN data from the two platform providers for accounts @TXCoastalWatchdog and @NuecesLocalNews under a law enforcement referral to FBI Cyber Division (referral number FB-2027-TXCYB-1148). The request will take 5–7 days to process. Separately, the CISA utility investigation team (T8) has already identified ASN 198765 as the hosting block for KESTREL VPN exit nodes used in the grid intrusion. The two investigative threads are running in parallel but have not yet been cross-referenced. This is the hidden connection point: when the FBI returns IP data showing @TXCoastalWatchdog and @NuecesLocalNews resolved to ASN 198765, the two threads will converge.

Household damage assessments are slowed by spill-zone access limits, flooded roads and the scale of damage; the state formally asks FEMA to add Individual Assistance; advocates say families without savings are waiting.

CBECC call volume returns to near-normal levels on D+28. Volume is 380 calls/day — slightly above pre-storm baseline (310/day) due to ongoing recovery activity. Director Escamilla-Voss issues an after-action summary noting that CBECC handled 44,291 calls on all lines (911 and ten-digit) over D0 through D+28, compared with a normal 28-day volume of approximately 8,680 calls — a 5.1x total volume increase. The boil water notice ends on D+42, the power restoration completes D+35, and by D+45 call volume returns to pre-storm baseline.

SCADA isolation: following 10 days of investigation under SI-2027-CC-001, CBPWA's incident response team (supplemented by Vantage Security Systems senior support engineer Marcus Teitelbaum-Park) confirms that GW-SYS-JMP-01 is compromised and that the ClearPath VPN jump host has been used as the pivot point for all OT-network historian and relay config access. At 08:00Z D+28, with ERCOT and TCEQ emergency coordination, CBPWA executes a controlled SCADA isolation: GW-SYS-JMP-01 is taken offline, the ClearPath VPN service is suspended, and the historian server GW-SRV-HIST-01 is isolated from the external-facing IT network. All 94 suppressed alarms in the DCS suppression list are restored. The relay config changes at SUB-02 are identified and reverification of all five substation relay settings begins. Sentinel Edge alert volume returns toward baseline; the C2 beacon from GW-WS-IT-04 goes silent within 2 hours (host isolated).

Gastroenteritis admissions decline to 18 per day across both hospitals (D+28 baseline), approaching pre-storm endemic levels. SRMC census is at 95% (475 patients) — below licensed capacity for the first time since D0. BCMC is at 89% (249 patients). The decline follows the Districts 3–4 boil-water notice taking hold in both languages; Zone 4 pressure itself only begins to recover on D+28, when the pump setpoint is restored (GW-EVT-014). Total cluster admissions: 1,820 patients across both facilities over 13 days. No deaths attributed directly to the gastroenteritis cluster, though 4 elderly patients with severe dehydration experienced prolonged hospitalizations. SRMC charge nurse Ana Lucía Montoya-Reyes leads a debriefing of the clinical response in a voice-recorded handoff session, noting that the cluster disproportionately affected elderly, pediatric, and dialysis-dependent patients in Districts 3–4.

CBPWA, on CISA guidance, isolates GW-SYS-SCADA-01 from all external network connectivity and GW-SYS-JMP-01 is taken offline. All five substations switch to manual relay operations. FAC-UTL-01 Pump P-3 setpoint is manually restored to 85 psi; Pump P-4 feeder supply restored from a temporary generator. Zone 4 pressure begins rising. Governor issues a supplemental emergency declaration covering the cyber component.

Governor has amended the existing Hurricane Rafael disaster declaration to include a cyber emergency component covering Corpus Christi utility infrastructure. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has deployed a cybersecurity rapid response team to assist local and state authorities. The affected utility has isolated its control systems as a precautionary measure; field crews are managing operations manually. The Governor's office emphasized that the water supply remains safe for boiled use and that electric restoration continues.

The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center today reported that Hurricane Rafael emergency call volume has returned to near-normal levels, with 380 calls received yesterday — approaching the pre-storm daily baseline of 310 calls. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss said the center is beginning a transition back to normal staffing over the next two weeks. 'Our dispatchers have shown extraordinary dedication over the past four weeks. The scale and duration of this response was unprecedented for our center, and I am incredibly proud of every person who answered calls, coordinated rescues, and kept working through the most demanding conditions I have seen in my career.' Director Escamilla-Voss noted that CBECC handled more than 44,200 calls in the four weeks after landfall, about five times the normal volume. The center is retaining all call records and audio as part of its standard after-action review process. Mutual aid units from San Patricio and Bee County will begin scaling back their support beginning October 14.

Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority has taken precautionary steps to isolate portions of its operational technology network following the identification of unauthorized access to network systems. These measures are being taken as part of an ongoing security investigation. The isolation is expected to cause no disruption to power or water service for CBPWA customers. CBPWA is cooperating with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and other relevant authorities. CBPWA emphasizes that the investigation is ongoing and no conclusions should be drawn about the nature or origin of the access at this time.

The city's weekly boil-water update at 09:00 CDT D+30 is issued simultaneously in English and Spanish — the first simultaneous bilingual public alert in the entire Rafael response sequence, following an internal directive issued D+22 after the LULAC complaint. Both notices stay in force: the citywide notice until pump repairs and testing are finished (lifted D+39) and the Districts 3 and 4 notice (lifted D+42). KNCB airs the update in real time. OEM announces a systematic review of the NCLAS contract and commits to simultaneous release for all future life-safety alerts. KNCB's 24-hour emergency format scales back to 18 hours beginning D+30, with normal music programming restored overnight.

Counter-UAS assessment and program announcement: Sentinel Airspace Inc. (fictional counter-UAS vendor) completes a site survey and publishes an unclassified counter-UAS program proposal for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor. The proposal recommends a 7-node RF detection and direction-finding network covering the Port of Corpus Christi, GW-FAC-SUB-01, and the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. Estimated drone detection probability at the thresholds relevant to the pre-storm sorties (DJI-class, 400-600 ft AGL, encrypted link): 73% with existing buoy network, 94% with the proposed Sentinel Airspace ground network upgrade. The assessment notes that the pre-storm sorties would have been detected with 91% probability by the proposed network. CBPWA CISO Dr. Al-Rasheed-Obinna (from T18) is cited as endorsing the proposal for the substation component.
Ship channel partly reopens; Gulf Provider's berth delayed by the anchorage backlog until D+33
Shoreline cleanup continues; the inner ship channel stays restricted for vessel decontamination until D+44

Ground truth (hidden): FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency opens Operation Sandbar following receipt of FEMA ECIMS suspicious activity flag SA-2027-TX-4471 (auto-routed D+33 but reviewed D+30 due to a parallel referral from Sabine National Insurance's Special Investigations Unit which flagged 47 LPH-related commercial claims with identical damage narratives). FBI case agent Special Agent Darnell Okafor-Reyes (fictional) is assigned as case lead. Texas DPS Criminal Investigations is brought in as co-investigator. The operation name is classified; it will not be made public until D+90.
Ship channel partly reopens; spill decontamination keeps the inner channel restricted; anchorage backlog delays relief cargo including MV Gulf Provider.

The Port of Corpus Christi Authority announced today that the Corpus Christi Ship Channel has partly reopened to commercial traffic, 30 days after Hurricane Rafael closed it. The Coast Guard cleared the outer and bay reaches of the channel after surveys of channel depth and aids to navigation. The inner channel remains restricted while vessels and berths affected by the Inner Harbor oil spill are decontaminated; no date has been set for lifting that restriction. Ships waiting at the offshore anchorage will be brought in by priority, and the backlog will delay some cargo, including relief shipments. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves said: 'We are grateful for the patience of our customers and maritime partners. The port team, together with the Coast Guard, NOAA and our contractor crews, worked extraordinary hours to restore safe navigation after one of the most demanding storm responses in our history.' Six port security cameras along the Inner Harbor remain offline pending replacement parts. The Coast Guard investigation into the tanker oil release remains open.

BOIL WATER NOTICES REMAIN IN EFFECT — weekly update. / LOS AVISOS DE HERVIR AGUA SIGUEN VIGENTES — actualización semanal. The Corpus Christi Water Department announces that the citywide boil water notice issued September 18, 2027 and the Boil Water Notice issued September 26, 2027 for Water Districts 3 and 4 both remain in effect as of 9:00 a.m. today, October 14, 2027. Replacement pump parts for the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant have not yet arrived, and neither notice can be lifted until repairs are complete and water quality testing meets all state and federal standards. Continue to bring water to a rolling boil before drinking, cooking, making ice or brushing teeth. This update is being released in English and Spanish at the same time. / La Ciudad de Corpus Christi anuncia que el aviso de hervir agua para toda la ciudad, emitido el 18 de septiembre de 2027, y el aviso emitido el 26 de septiembre de 2027 para los Distritos de Agua 3 y 4 siguen vigentes a las 9:00 a.m. de hoy, 14 de octubre de 2027. Las piezas de repuesto para las bombas de la planta O.N. Stevens aún no han llegado. Siga hirviendo el agua antes de beberla, cocinar, hacer hielo o cepillarse los dientes. Este aviso se publica en inglés y en español al mismo tiempo.

DISASTER CLAIMS SURGE UPDATE — October 14, 2027: The Texas Department of Insurance and the Insurance Council of Texas report that Hurricane Rafael has generated approximately 187,000 property insurance claims across Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties as of October 14, representing an estimated $2.1 billion in insured losses. This ranks as the second-largest coastal insured loss event in Texas since Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Claims volume in the Corpus Christi metropolitan area exceeds industry catastrophe response models by approximately 23 percent. TDI has activated its Disaster Response Team and deployed 12 field claim examiners. The department notes an elevated pattern of large commercial property claims in Districts 3-5 that is under review. Adjusters are reporting difficulty verifying pre-storm property values in certain commercial portfolios. Homeowners and commercial property owners are reminded that Texas law requires insurers to acknowledge claims within 15 days and pay or deny within 15 business days of receiving all claim documentation. Residents experiencing claim delays should contact TDI at (800) 252-3439. TDI is tracking contractor fraud complaints and coordinating with the Texas DPS.

TDI ACTIVATES CLAIMS FRAUD TASK FORCE — October 14, 2027: Texas Department of Insurance Commissioner announces the activation of a Disaster Claims Fraud Task Force for Nueces County following Hurricane Rafael. The task force, operating in coordination with the FBI and Texas DPS, will focus on detecting and preventing fraudulent insurance claims arising from the storm. TDI has identified patterns of concern including clusters of large commercial property claims with similar damage narratives, inflated pre-storm appraisals, and claims for total losses on properties that sustained only partial damage. TDI emphasizes that filing a fraudulent insurance claim is a third-degree felony in Texas, punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and fines up to $10,000. Insurers are reminded of their obligation to refer suspected fraud to TDI's Fraud Unit. TDI is working with the Insurance Council of Texas to establish a Nueces County claims database to identify duplicate and suspicious claims across carriers. Legitimate policyholders are encouraged to cooperate with claim investigations and to report any third party who pressured them into filing inflated claims.

The ship channel partly reopens (EVT-0401; PUB-058, PUB-123): the outer and bay reaches are cleared for deep-draft traffic while the inner channel stays restricted for vessel decontamination until D+44 (EVT-0410). The port's surveillance network is back in service in time for the night that follows: 8 of 14 fixed cameras are online and both radar buoys are reporting. On D+31 it records Halcyon Drift's 14-hour AIS silence, a vessel broadcasting FV Pelican Ridge's identity at the anchorage, and radar contacts with no AIS match — two hulls side by side at the anchorage and one loitering about 2 nm off the entrance channel (EVT-0402, EVT-0403, EVT-0411).

FBI Cyber Division returns IP records to TDEM and Coastal Alert team. @TXCoastalWatchdog's account activity from D-5 through D+22 resolves to source IPs in the 198.51.47.0/24 block — ASN 198765. @NuecesLocalNews resolves to 198.51.48.0/24 — also ASN 198765. The CISA utility investigation lead, upon receiving the cross-reference notification from FBI, confirms: same ASN, same /16 supernet as the KESTREL VPN exit nodes used in the grid intrusion. The connection is classified at this stage. TDEM is briefed under NDA. The two accounts are suspended by the platforms following FBI notification. 45 of the original 47 pre-positioned accounts are still active at D+30 (two were removed by platforms earlier for TOS violations).
Halcyon Drift's AIS goes silent for 14 h; a vessel broadcasting MMSI-SYN-0457 appears at the anchorage while the real Pelican Ridge reports 600 nm away
Radar pass shows an unidentified hull loitering 2 nm off the entrance channel for 40 minutes during Halcyon Drift's AIS gap: DEV-01 and DEV-02 are laid
Radar shows two hulls side by side, one with no AIS match: fuel transfer to Barge 44
Barge 44 delivers 380 m³ of fuel up the ship channel to SUP-0390; deliveries to NAS Corpus Christi invoiced from D+33

The Texas Division of Emergency Management, working with federal partners, has identified and referred to law enforcement a network of social media accounts that disseminated false public safety information during Hurricane Rafael. The accounts distributed incorrect evacuation shelter locations, false road closure information, and misleading content about utility restoration and federal investigations. TDEM's social media monitoring tool, Coastal Alert, detected anomalous posting behavior consistent with coordinated inauthentic behavior. TDEM has referred account information to the FBI and has coordinated with social media platforms on account review. Members of the public who encountered false shelter or evacuation information during the Rafael response are asked to report it to TDEM's public information line at 512-424-2208. TDEM reminds the public to verify emergency information through official sources: NuecesCountyOEM.org, 2-1-1 Texas, and local broadcast stations designated in the Corpus Christi Emergency Alert System.

The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority today announced a joint counter-unmanned aircraft initiative for the Corpus Christi critical infrastructure corridor, following a recommendation in the FAA-CBP joint report on pre-storm unauthorized drone activity. The initiative will deploy an RF-sensing detection and direction-finding network at multiple sites across the port and utility infrastructure corridor, operated in coordination with the FAA and CBP Air and Marine Operations. Sentinel Airspace Inc. has been selected as the technology provider following a competitive evaluation. The network is expected to be operational within 90 days. Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center today released their joint Hurricane Rafael Hospital Operations After-Action Report. The report documents the response of both facilities from September 11 through October 14, 2027. Combined, the two hospitals treated 4,217 hurricane-related patients over that period. The response involved two distinct patient surge waves: a trauma wave from landfall on September 14 through September 21, during which SRMC operated at up to 140% licensed bed capacity on generator power, and a waterborne disease cluster from September 29 through October 12, during which 1,820 patients were treated for Cryptosporidium and Giardia infection. The cluster was geographically concentrated in Water Districts 3 and 4. The report notes that early-cluster admissions disproportionately included patients from Spanish-dominant households, a pattern the report identifies as potentially related to the delay in Spanish-language boil-water notification. No patient deaths were directly attributable to the hospital surge response. The report recommends expanded generator diesel reserves, pre-positioned water testing capabilities, and enhanced multilingual patient communication protocols for future mass casualty and public health emergency events.

OPERATION SANDBAR — 14 ARRESTED IN HURRICANE RAFAEL DISASTER FRAUD SCHEME — December 13, 2027: The Federal Bureau of Investigation Houston Division, FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency, and the Texas Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division today announced 14 arrests in connection with a large-scale disaster fraud scheme that targeted federal disaster assistance programs and private insurers following Hurricane Rafael. The defendants, led by Corpus Christi resident Renaldo Carver-Mossbach, 44, are accused of fraudulently inflating insurance values on 230 properties before the storm and subsequently filing 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications claiming damage that did not occur or was dramatically overstated.
